questions.question: What is data parallelism?

options.text: Running the same model on different data subsets

questions.explanation: Data parallelism involves running the same model simultaneously on different subsets of the data.

questions.question: What is the main benefit of model parallelism?
questions.explanation: Model parallelism allows for training larger models that do not fit into the memory of a single device.

questions.question: What is the purpose of Fully Sharded Data Parallel (FSDP)?

options.text: To shard the model weights across devices

questions.explanation: FSDP shards the model's parameters across different devices to optimize memory usage.

questions.question: Order these steps to set up data parallel training:
questions.explanation: You must initialize the model first, then distribute the data, configure the optimizer, and finally set up the training loop.

questions.question: Which of the following is a common challenge with distributed training?
questions.explanation: Communication overhead is a significant challenge in distributed training as it can slow down the training process.

questions.question: Using model parallelism always leads to faster training times.
questions.explanation: Model parallelism can lead to slower training due to increased communication costs between devices.
